name: Sweden: Stockholm, Gotland and the Kungsleden
region: Sweden and Swedish Lapland, by train
tagline: Day train to Stockholm, night train to the Arctic, hut-to-hut above the treeline, and a medieval walled town on an island.

access.route: Train: Brussels→Hamburg→Copenhagen→Stockholm (about 13 h, or overnight from Hamburg); Norrland night train Stockholm→Abisko (17 h, couchettes)
Eurostar→Brussels→Hamburg→Copenhagen→Stockholm (two days or the Hamburg night train)

nightsNote: 4–8°C at the Kungsleden huts, 12°C in Stockholm
whyNotes: The furthest north you can get without a plane, and closest to the Alta Via rhythm: five days hut to hut with light packs, STF huts with saunas, then a city with world-class museums. Gotland adds the history.
fitNotes: Highest point 1,150 m, 15–22°C, long light. Crowds: Visby during Medieval Week (early August) and the Abisko trailhead on July weekends; the trail itself empties after day one. Mosquitoes in Lapland in July are real; August is better.

blocks.name: Stockholm
blocks.place: Vasa, Skansen, Nordic Museum, Fotografiska, Gamla Stan
see: Vasa museum (the 17th-century warship, intact)
Skansen open-air museum and the Nordic Museum on Djurgården
Gamla Stan early, Royal Palace, Storkyrkan
Fotografiska and Moderna Museet
Archipelago ferry to Vaxholm or Fjäderholmarna for an evening
blocks.note: Arrival by day train via Copenhagen. Stay on Södermalm or Kungsholmen: cheaper, local, 15 minutes from everything.

blocks.name: Uppsala + Sigtuna
blocks.place: Cathedral, Gamla Uppsala royal mounds, Linnaeus garden
see: Gamla Uppsala mounds and museum
Uppsala cathedral and Gustavianum
Linnaeus garden
Sigtuna, Sweden's oldest town, on the way back

blocks.name: Visby, Gotland
blocks.place: Hanseatic walled town (UNESCO), rauk sea stacks, 90 medieval churches
see: The 3.5 km town wall and the church ruins
Gotland museum (picture stones, the Spillings hoard)
Fårö rauks and Bergman's island
Cycle the country churches; Lummelunda cave
blocks.note: Ferry from Nynäshamn (3 h). Medieval Week, usually the second week of August, fills the island; otherwise July is busy with Swedes, August quiet.

blocks.name: Gothenburg
blocks.place: West-coast port, Konstmuseum, the southern archipelago
see: Göteborgs Konstmuseum (Nordic painting)
Haga and the fish church
Car-free southern archipelago by ferry

blocks.name: Kungsleden: Abisko to Nikkaluokta
blocks.place: 5 days, STF huts with saunas, Tjäktja pass 1,150 m, Kebnekaise base
see: Abisko to Abiskojaure, Alesjaure, Tjäktja, Sälka, Singi, Kebnekaise fjällstation
Boat shortcuts on two lakes if legs are tired
Kebnekaise summit (2,097 m) from the fjällstation for the siblings
Sauna and lake swim at every hut
blocks.note: Night train Stockholm→Abisko counts as a night's lodging. Huts take no booking for sleeping (nobody is turned away) but have simple dorms; Kebnekaise fjällstation has rooms.

blocks.name: Abisko day walks
blocks.place: Abisko canyon, Kårsavagge, Njulla by chairlift
see: Aurora Sky Station chairlift to Njulla (view of Lapporten)
Abisko canyon and the Kårsavagge valley
Lake Torneträsk shore

blocks.name: Höga Kusten (High Coast)
blocks.place: UNESCO uplift coast: Skuleskogen, Slåttdalsskrevan, the High Coast trail
see: Skuleskogen national park and the Slåttdalsskrevan crevice
Two or three day-stages of the Höga Kusten trail with a cabin or B&B each night
Ulvön island and the fermented-herring museum
Skuleberget via ferrata for the siblings
blocks.note: Quiet, cheap, 5 h by train north of Stockholm. The best under-visited hiking in southern Sweden.

blocks.name: Stockholm archipelago: Utö, Grinda, Finnhamn
blocks.place: Island hopping on the Waxholm boats, forest and rock walks, kayaks
see: Utö mines trail and cycling
Finnhamn nature reserve walk
Kayak from Grinda
Hostel or cabin nights on the islands

blocks.name: Dalarna: Fulufjället
blocks.place: Njupeskär falls, Old Tjikko (9,500-year-old spruce), fjäll plateau
see: Njupeskär, Sweden's highest waterfall
Old Tjikko guided walk
Plateau loop to the Rösjöstugorna cabins

blocks.name: Kvikkjokk and the edge of Sarek
see: Kvikkjokk delta boat
Kungsleden south to Pårte hut and back
Guided day into Sarek's edge with a Sámi guide
blocks.note: Wilder and emptier than Abisko; needs a guide for anything beyond the marked trail.

notes: Kungsleden huts open until mid-September; midnight sun at Abisko until about 17 July, light nights all window.
Mosquitoes in Lapland peak in July and fade in August; carry a head net either way.
Swedish industrial holidays run to early August: Gotland and the archipelago are busiest before then.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
